ceiling_directive: Prove the high-probability bound U(G_n,k_n)=O(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)])—either through the stated Boolean radius-two operator estimate or a direct covariance-certificate argument—to match the new converse.
improvement_directive: Resolve oeq:boolean-operator by proving \|B_2(G_n)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_{\Pr}(d_n^{7/4}) uniformly for 3\le d_n=o(\sqrt n), or directly establish the resulting logarithmic Schur-certificate bound. This would turn the current logarithmic bracket into the requested full minimax order using the same design and estimand.
critique: The note proves an all-procedure lower bound of order d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)] and an attainable deterministic upper bound of order d_n^2/n, so the delivered result is a logarithmic bracket rather than the advertised full minimax frontier for diverging degrees. The sharper upper edge is conditional on oeq:boolean-operator, while the unconditional upper scale coincides with the closest comparator; therefore the field-contract claim of resolving the full order remains under-delivered, and the label thm:matched-frontier is stale over-claiming despite the theorem text's later disclaimer. The proposed finite compiler relies on n^{k_n} seed-tuple enumeration and supplies no complexity-controlled approximation or numerical demonstration, weakening the practical and reproducibility case for the prospective experiment. These unresolved rate and computation limitations keep the package below a field-level contribution and constrain the projected paper score.
